accepts.because: a turn from the surface. The caller MUST promote the channel identity to context.channel, or every chat of the colony lands on the channel `default`; and it MUST promote the round to context.audience_set if the closed sessions of this talky are to reach a memory, because the generation this turn opens is where the round is recorded
an operator-forced session sweep outside the night timer
one tool result, coming back from a tool cell the parent wired
an advisor's answer, coming back from a second agent

an errand the voice model handed the backend of its own accord, in a duplex call (welle-live, R-25-4). It arrives straight from the channel and NOT through a firewall, because a firewall's exit stamps `in_turn` and this is no turn of the conversation: the model keeps talking to the caller while this is worked on. The caller MUST promote `context.delegation_id` -- it is the correlation the answer travels back under -- and `context.engine`, which is what puts this agent into advise mode; without the engine the brain would answer the caller in prose nobody speaks. The collector assembles it exactly like `in_advice`, under role `delegation`, and keeps it out of both memory writers

a duplex voice session of a running call was renewed at its provider's limit (GH #896): `hop.call_id`, `hop.renewal_n`. It goes to `./curator` and nowhere else -- no round, no brain call: the curator puts the running conversation together without a model and the answer leaves as ONE `sidecar` section `context` carrying `hop.renewal_n`, on the edge every curator section leaves by, with `context.call_id` so the channel's `in_advise` finds the call

a memory bundle, coming back from whatever keeps this agent's memory. Since GH #895 a bundle whose `context.gap_ask` is set answers the curator's own lookup of a gap and goes to `./curator` (`in_gap_bundle`), never to the collector, which has no round for it

the brief of the turn's counterpart, coming back from whatever keeps this agent's record of people -- under GH #834 that is the member's `affinity`, and the member restamps its answer (or its error) onto this lane. It enters the collector like `in_bundle`: the third leg of a turn, waited for only when the collector's `brief_slots` is set
a round that ran out of iterations, swept by an operator

a durable `system.*` slot for this agent's brain -- the door in the wall (GH #458). This composite is sealed: an edge naming `./brain` is refused with `hive_port_boundary`, so until this lane existed there was no way at all for an identity to reach the brain from outside, and `affinity` could push into nowhere. Since talky@6.0.0 the pack enters `./curator` (GH #889), which holds it in its ledger and hands it to the brain as a system slot with the next call, and it is a LANE rather than a body flag because what lands in `system.*` stands in that ledger until something overwrites that exact path -- durable state of the agent, told apart from the evidence of one round by the topology and not by a key a model could have written. Body: `system` carrying one or more slot subtrees (what `affinity`'s push lane emits: the slots and NO turn beside them, so the update costs a write and not an inference, GH #263), or `slot` + `content` for a single one written by hand. Only `identity`, `persona`, `handover` and `instructions` may be written. `instructions` joined that list in GH #488: holding the charter out of the lane assumed it had another owner, and it had none -- nothing exported it and no template seeded it, so a rebuilt generation came up with an empty charter and answered as the vendor's default assistant. What guards it now is the edge that stamps the lane, drawn only where a brain may draw its OWN push edge, from a source whose single writer is `affinity`'s audited gate; anything else refuses the WHOLE pack with `slot_unknown`, an empty one with `pack_empty`. The owner is taken from `envelope.reply_to` and never from the body. PAIRED with `pack_ack` in `params.required_drains`: it answers unconditionally, and a push whose receipt nobody takes dead-letters after the sender was already told it was accepted

a pin of another hive for this brain's window (GH #916): `{pins: [{text, source, until?}], replace_sources?}`, handed unchanged to `./curator` on its own `in_pin` door, which writes it into the ledger and shows it in the window (`templates/curator/README.md`). `context.audience_set` travels with it untouched. Nothing answers it

a model package for the brain, pushed by the colony's llm-registry (GH #855): a PARAMS-ONLY body -- an empty `system` slot, no `messages` -- that the brain merges into its live params and answers with nothing. It goes from this path straight to `./brain`, past the collector: a params body is not a turn, and the collector has no business holding, stamping or dropping one. It is the one way a model package reaches the brain; the brain applies package keys only from a params-only message (GH #853), so a turn on any other lane cannot change the model it talks to. Draw it only from the registry's `update` lane, restamped `in_model`

the tool declarations coming back from a tools hive the parent wired (GH #464). Since talky@4.5.1 this composite ASKS what its tools look like instead of carrying a menu somebody typed: `./collector`'s `params.tools` is the list of names this agent declares it uses, the request leaves on `schemas`, and what arrives here is the answer -- `schemas[]` plus the names the hive had nothing under. The collector wraps each declaration in the provider envelope and writes the result into `./brain` as durable `system.tools`, so the menu costs one write per change and nothing per turn. PAIRED with `schemas`: a parent that draws one half of the pair and not the other has a composite that asks into nothing, or one that is answered at a door it does not have

a demand that this composite hand out the one store it owns that is not a conversation: the session ledger, the table that remembers which generation a channel is in the middle of. The lane crosses this level UNCHANGED and lands on the `in_export` of `./session-keeper` (session-keeper@2.1.0, GH #471), whose own walk decides what leaves and in what format; this composite reads no part and judges none. It carries no modifier for the same reason `in_import` does not: the lane is named the same on both sides of this boundary, and a rename onto itself would hide the pairing from the drain probe. Until GH #475 the keeper answered the lane and nothing above it ever forwarded one, so a member rebuilt from its own export came back knowing everything it had been told and greeting the person it had been talking to for a year as a stranger

one part of such a document, for a keeper that is already RUNNING. It is the other half of `in_export` and the return leg of the same document: `sessions/seed` was read once, when the keeper's `cell.db` was created, and is inert for ever after -- so a ledger walked out after that moment has no way back except a message. It crosses to `./session-keeper` unchanged (session-keeper@2.1.0). The body is ONE export part, and applying the same part twice leaves the same state, which is what makes a partial transfer repairable by repeating it (GH #475)

the answer half of the same lane (GH #560): the broker's `ack` for `vault.deliver` carrying the sealed box, renamed at the boundary to the name this rim knows it by. It lands on `./brain` and on nothing else -- the box is sealed against the ephemeral key of the cell that asked, so a delivery anywhere else is a box nobody can open plus a receipt the asker never gets. Address the edge with `hop.grant_id`, which the broker stamps: one grant per consumer, or two brains are handed each other's rounds

the mutation receipt on its last hop, GH #553: the graph moved, and the collector inside this composite is what has to hear it -- the tool menu is re-asked on it. The lane keeps ONE name from the mutation door down to here, and this rim is a plain door for it: the composite's own edge carries it to `./collector`, which turns it into its internal `in_menu_tick`. It replaces a five-minute poll timer that used to sit inside the collector, and the boot receipt is the first ask, so an agent has its menu before its first turn. Derived from collector@4.0.0

a question an observer asks about this brain's window (GH #926): the hop keys of the curator's own `in_stats` (`stats_tag`, `stats_from`, `stats_to`, `stats_kinds`, `stats_samples`), handed unchanged to `./curator`, which counts its ledger and answers on `stats`

emits.because: the finished turn, for the reply sink. Two sorts travel here and hop.round_capped tells them apart: a real answer and a round that hit max_iter. Since collector@2.1.1 a THIRD sort travels here and it is told apart by `hop.degraded`, not by `round_capped` (which such a message does not carry): a turn that could not be assembled at all because the store refused a read or a write (GH #343). `hop.store_error` carries the store's `error_code`, `hop.store_operation` the op it refused, and the text names both. A parent that renders an answer must branch on `degraded` -- without it a failure reads as a real reply. Since `collector@4.4.0` every answer also says how the completion behind it ended (GH #843): `hop.finish_reason` (`stop`, `length`, or empty where the collector knows no reason -- a capped round's digest, a store report) and `hop.truncated`, `"1"` when the completion was cut on `length`. A `length` finish goes through the splitter since `talky@5.4.0`, so a cut answer leaves without its sidecar; a consumer that must not pass on a half sentence refuses or marks it on `truncated`
a closed session as one write batch, for wherever a day belongs. It carries context.channel and context.audience_set of the conversation -- off the generation row, not off the sweep that ended it

ONE finished turn per message after every stored turn and every stored answer -- never a batch (GH #298, ruling Q11): one user/assistant turn in messages[], hop.turn_id '<session_id>#<index>', hop.turn_index and hop.happened_at beside it, which is the shape a memory hive's episode lane reads. An occasion may carry several messages, one per turn not yet written. On unless the instance switches the turn_write knob of `./curator`'s writer off

one section of the block a turn's answer carried, as the model wrote it: hop.section names the section, hop.turn_id the round it answered (GH #916), the body carries {messages: [], section, payload}. ONE message PER SECTION -- never repaired, never re-serialised, and never judged here, so a parent distributes on hop.section and a section this composite has never heard of needs no change to it. Since talky@5.1.0 this port replaces `extraction`, which carried exactly one thing (the memory annotation, as raw text) and is now the section `memory` on this route (GH #605); a parent still wired on `hop.route == 'extraction'` writes nothing. Since talky@4.1.0 this is how per-turn extraction travels at all: it is NOT a tool call any more, so a parent that wired the old `hop.tool_name == 'remember'` lane rewires it to this route too. The curator's own sections (`window`, `gap`) never travel here, and `memory` travels through the curator unchanged (GH #892). It is a lane and not an obligation: without the block contract in the brain's instructions there is nothing to cut and nothing ever travels here. Since GH #895 one more section leaves here that no answer carried: in a duplex call `./curator` sends a gap's find as `fact` for the voice model

a memory read this turn needs: the collector's per-turn ask, whose question `./curator` builds out of the wall since GH #895 (same hop keys), and the curator's own lookup of a gap of an answer, which lifts `hop.gap_ask` into `context.gap_ask` on the way out so its bundle comes back to the curator
a brief about the counterpart this turn is with (GH #834): raised by the collector at the turn's opening when `brief_slots` is set and the turn carries `context.counterpart`

a tool call for a cell the parent wired; hop.tool_name says which one. Since talky@4.2.1 the exit is a GUARDED DEFAULT edge (GH #283, ruling Q1): `{"from": "./dispatcher", "to": ".", "default": true, "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'tool'"}`. It is consulted only when NO ordinary edge out of ./dispatcher fired for the message. Since talky@6.0.0 no name is reserved here (GH #889). `memory_recall` was reserved until talky@5.0.0: this composite served it out of its own collector and declared its schema by hand, and since GH #552 it is an ORDINARY tool name -- the member's memory hive declares it, answers it, and this default edge carries the call out like any other. Two properties keep it honest, and both were measured against this tree rather than assumed. FIRST, the guard is not decoration: ./dispatcher emits four sorts (calls, result, answer, tool) and suppression is SENDER-WIDE, so an unguarded default would try to carry calls/result/answer outward whenever nothing ordinary happened to fire for them; the condition names the one lane this default consumes and leaves the rest to no_route. SECOND, the no-tee requirement: ./dispatcher has four out-edges here (calls, result and answer into ./collector, plus this one) and every ordinary one of them is conditioned on its own lane -- there is NO unconditional tee. If the set ever grows one (a logger, a tap, a mirror), it must be conditioned on its own routes, or it silences this default for every tool call and the parent's tool cells go dark. The sender inventory of the whole composite, for the same reason: nine senders (., ./session-keeper, ./schemas, ./collector, ./curator, ./brain, ./splitter, ./dispatcher, ./errors) over 39 edges since 6.0.0, seven of which reach `.` (./collector four times, ./curator four times -- write, turn_write, pack_ack, model_refused --, ./session-keeper twice, ./brain for a refused model, ./splitter for the sidecar, ./dispatcher for this default, ./errors for error) -- and the sender-wide rule means an edge a PARENT draws from ./talky/dispatcher counts here too
a normalised failure report. The parent MUST wire it -- unwired it dead-letters, loudly

a model package pushed through `in_model` that the brain refused (GH #863): its error, with the brain's own path in `hop.refused_subscriber` and the model the push named in `hop.refused_model`, leaves here instead of on `error` -- a refused push is no conversation's failure, and `./errors` never sees it. The builder draws one edge from here to the registry's container, which carries it back to the registry's `in_refused` lane; without one the refusal dead-letters `no_route`, loudly

the receipt of one pack, unconditionally -- accepted and refused alike (GH #458). `hop.pack_owner` is the sender off the envelope, `hop.pack_slots` what was named, `hop.error_code` empty or `slot_unknown` / `pack_empty`, `hop.pack_unknown` the slots that were refused. It answers even on success because from the sending side a push that landed and a push that reached nothing are otherwise the same silence, which is the failure class `docs/development-rules.md` § 2c names. Every key is present and empty rather than absent, so a CEL guard on an edge never fails on a missing hop key

the tool names this agent declares it uses, for a tools hive's `in_schemas` door (GH #464). The body is `{"tools": [...]}` and nothing else; `["*"]` asks for everything that hive has. It leaves on a tick rather than per turn, and the hive keeps no record of who asked -- whoever designed this composite's instance decided what it uses, and that decision lives in `./collector`'s `params.tools` where the rest of its contract is. Unwired it dead-letters once per tick, which is why the pair with `in_menu` is one decision and not two

the keeper inside this composite has written its session ledger out completely, and says so itself (GH #555): `hop.export_hive` names the hive, `hop.seed_dir` the directory relative to the fence its store declares. Carried out of this composite unchanged -- this level owns no part of the document and never did

the receipt of one applied import part, raised by `./session-keeper` and carried out of this composite unchanged: `hop.rows_written` counts the inserts it dispatched, so zero means the target already had every row. Since 0.30.0 the lane carries NOTHING ELSE -- an export writes its own files and reports on `export_done` (GH #555), so the `dump_kind` key that told the two apart is gone with the distinction. Drain it with a PLAIN `hop.route == 'dump'` edge -- an edge that tests a second key reads as no drain under the required_drains probe

the ask half of the credential lane (GH #421/#452/#560): the brain that spends a grant holds no bearer of its own, mints an ephemeral X25519 recipient key per ask and sends the grant handle out with it. This is a V-LANE (GH #559) and `at` is what makes it one: `params.ports` stays literally `[]`, and `./brain` is the one address this sealed rim opens for this one lane -- an opening the template pronounces about ITSELF, never one a caller helps itself to. Whoever draws the edge points it at the access hive that owns the person's keys and stamps `context.requester` on it, because the requester comes from the EDGE and never from the body (R-AC-1)

the curator's answer to one `in_stats`, unchanged: `stats: {from, to, counts, samples, truncated}` with `hop.stats_tag` echoed, `hop.error_code` and `hop.detail` (`templates/curator/README.md`). One answer per question; the asker matches it by its tag

required_drains.because: a pack answers unconditionally -- with the slots it wrote, or with the code that refused it. Undrained, every push dead-letters its own receipt and the sender's `sent_at` stamp records a delivery nobody can confirm: the write happened or it did not, and no reader can tell which. Drain it with a PLAIN `hop.route == 'pack_ack'` edge
the export IS this lane -- wired without it, the keeper's store writes its seed set and nobody is ever told where, or that it finished at all. Taken from the level below, which pairs the same two

the receipt of an applied part is the only positive signal an import has -- undrained, nobody ever learns whether a transfer landed. Taken from session-keeper@2.1.0, which pairs the same two lanes one level down

edges.condition: has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'in_tool' || hop.route == 'in_advice' || hop.route == 'in_delegation' || hop.route == 'in_bundle' || hop.route == 'in_briefing' || hop.route == 'in_round_sweep' || hop.route == 'in_menu') && !(hop.route == 'in_bundle' && has(context.gap_ask) && context.gap_ask != '')

description.purpose: Scope marker of the talky composite: bundles the session keeper, the context collector, the curator, the brain and the tool dispatcher behind ONE ingress, ONE reply exit, ONE write exit and ONE error drain. Everything the first production rollout wired by hand -- the stamp, the seam, the dispatcher lanes, the loopback with restore_ttl, the close path -- is an internal edge here. Since talky@4.3.0 (GH #447) the close batch leaves on the write port as it is: the member above the talky turns it into the memory hive's close pass, and what the next generation needs of it comes back through the recall bundle -- beside the one call a close costs in here, off the hot path: the curator condenses the closed session into a handover note through its own summarizer (GH #896), and the next generation reads it on its first call as `history.handover`. Since talky@4.5.1 (GH #458) it has ONE more door and it is the one it never had: `in_pack`, through which a durable `system.*` slot -- an identity, a persona, a handover -- reaches the brain from outside a composite that is otherwise sealed against exactly that. Since talky@4.5.1 (GH #464) it also stops carrying a tool menu somebody typed: `./collector`'s `params.tools` names the tools this agent uses, the names leave on `schemas` and the declarations come back on `in_menu` to be written into the brain as durable `system.tools`. Since talky@4.5.1 (GH #475) it passes two more doors straight through to that keeper -- `in_export` and `in_import` -- and carries the keeper's `dump` back out: the sessions are the one thing in here a member cannot recompute, and until this the lane stopped at a hive nothing above it forwarded to.
description.use_when: One per conversational agent. Instantiate it in the same mutation that wires the four ports plus the per-instance tool lanes; the composite is an island until an edge crosses into it.
description.not_in_scope: No tool cells (they are wired per instance on hop.tool_name), no memory hive, no surface proxy, no drain cell -- with ONE exception since 4.2.0, and it is a boundary rather than a gap: the tools this composite IMPLEMENTED were served by the collector inside it and routed by this template's own edges (GH #55); since talky@6.0.0 there are none (GH #889). RETRACTED with the same bump: up to 4.1.1 this line read `The brain's identity, instructions and tool schemas live in its own cell.db -- the composite carries the topology, never the persona`. The schema half no longer holds. A tool the composite IMPLEMENTS is topology, and its schema ships with the composite; a tool the PARENT wires is the agent, and the composite carries neither its schema nor its lane. So the composite carries the schemas of those two tools and of no others. Identity, instructions and every per-agent tool stay the brain's own cell.db -- the composite still carries no persona.
